subject: Intermittent reply lag impacting chat sessions — tailored mitigation plan
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex@fastretail.co>, support@fastretail.co
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -0000
Subject: Intermittent reply lag impacting chat sessions — tailored mitigation plan

Hi Alex / FastRetail support team,

Thanks for the heads-up this morning — we see the same symptom on our side: intermittent increases in token-level latency for streaming chat (clients observing bursts of 800–1,200ms per token vs baseline ~120–200ms). Impact appears concentrated on a subset of edge nodes in us-west.

Short-term mitigations we've applied or recommend immediately (low-risk):
- Route-level change: rolling traffic off the hot edge shard to adjacent healthy shards (already started for 30% of traffic).
- Client-side: switch to polling fallback (non-stream) for critical user flows where total response completeness matters more than near-realtime tokens.
- Server-side toggles: temporarily reduce max_concurrent_batch_size for the affected shard from 32 -> 12 to avoid batch amplification during token bursts.
- Cache: enable aggressive prefix KV cache for repeated conversation turns.

We attach a short telemetry dump (diagnostic_telemetry_2027-04-10.csv) illustrating the spike windows. We'll push a small edge runtime patch (edge_batching_patch.diff) that limits batching amplification and adds additional exponential backoff on token flush. Expected rollout within 3 hours.

Ask from you: can you confirm whether FastRetail can toggle to non-stream endpoints for the busiest customer-facing flows for the next 4–6 hours? If not, we'll prioritize a canary rollback for the shard and raise capacity on dedicated pools as an alternate mitigation.

I'll follow up with a brief post-incident note when we have the root-cause. Apologies for the disruption — we know streaming responsiveness is core to your UX.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: diagnostic_telemetry_2027-04-10.csv (CSV, ~1.2MB), edge_batching_patch.diff (text, 3KB)

Naomi — thanks for the quick reply and the mitigation steps.

We are seeing a spike in support tickets about slow chat replies impacting checkout help flows. We can temporarily switch the checkout help to the non-stream endpoint; engineering will need exact header/route names to change (we use the route alias fastretail-chat-live). If you can confirm the recommended fallback route and whether any tokenization/response-size adjustments are needed on our side, we can flip it within 30–45 minutes.

Also: do you have guidance on client-side retry/backoff parameters? Some of our engineers are worried about generating extra load if everyone retries aggressively.

— Alex
Head of Product, FastRetail

Subject: Re: Intermittent reply lag impacting chat sessions — tailored mitigation plan

Naomi / Steph — quick internal note on what we're seeing from the runtime side:

Initial signal: a subtle scheduling bug that allows batches to grow when token-emission spikes align with a periodic background GC on the edge runtime. On impacted shards that produced larger-than-expected batches, the kernel selection occasionally fell back to a slower path (quantization-padding fallback) which amplified per-token latency.

Immediate ops actions (in progress):
- Canary rollback of the recent scheduler change on 1 hot shard (rolled at 17:10 UTC).
- Force re-route: moved ~30% of FastRetail traffic off the hot shard to adjacent healthy shards.
- Deploy patch: edge_batching_patch.diff limits batch aggregation during token spikes and prevents the padding fallback for short bursts. Canary to 10% traffic now, full rollout if telemetry looks good.
- Monitoring: added a token-latency alert at 250ms median over 1 minute for the affected routing policy.

Risk/notes: the canary rollback reduces the chance of repeated amplification quickly; full rollout of the patch should stabilize token latency but may increase average CPU on some edge nodes (we're watching cost vs. latency tradeoffs).

I'll stay on the thread and give a go/no-go when canary metrics are stable (target 60 minutes).

— Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:17:00 -0000
Subject: Update: edge patch rolled, recommendations for FastRetail clients

Alex / FastRetail team — quick update and steps to reduce user-visible lag going forward.

What we changed (completed):
- Rolled patch to affected shards (full rollout at 08:50 UTC). Median token latency returned to baseline for canary users; overall incident window closed.
- Reverted scheduler change on the one hot shard which eliminated the pathological batch growth.
- Added a monitoring alert and an automated routing rule to throttle batch sizes if median per-token latency exceeds 250ms for >2 consecutive minutes.

Short client-side guidance (recommended):
- Fallback: If you can, keep the non-stream fallback for checkout help for 6–12 hours while we monitor. Route alias: fastretail-chat-live -> use endpoint POST /v1/chat/completions?stream=false
- Retry/backoff: exponential backoff with base 250ms, max retries 2. Use jitter (±25%) to avoid synchronized retries.
- Max tokens: if you control prompt length, prefer reducing max_tokens by ~15% for the next 24 hours to reduce peak emission bursts.

Attached: telemetry CSV and the patch diff we deployed. We'll publish a short post-incident note with a timeline and RCA by EOD Pacific (link to draft incident doc above). If you'd like a quick 20-minute sync to walk through the toggles, I'm available today at 17:00 PDT.

Thanks for the rapid coordination — please let us know when you've toggled the fallback so we can confirm traffic patterns.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: diagnostic_telemetry_2027-04-10.csv, edge_batching_patch.diff
